summary: The fixed-key fiber reduction withstands the skeptical check: deleting its common pair preserves distinctness and lifts residual sunflowers to actual four-set sunflowers. The revised singleton-trace explanation needs one precise wording repair: the contradiction uses the two original members and R, whereas the sentence currently names the deleted residues. The formal inherited proof performs the correct lift, so this is a minor proof-exposition issue rather than a defect in the theorem.
required_revisions: In Section 4 replace “disjoint residues together with R would form a sunflower” with “if two residues were disjoint, their two original members together with R would form a sunflower with core the deleted point” (or equivalent wording that explicitly lifts back to members of H).

findings.statement: The new singleton exact-trace sentence describes a sunflower using deleted triple residues and the anchor R; those residues need not be members of H, so that wording omits the lift needed for the contradiction.
findings.disposition: Name the two original four-set members and the singleton core. The formal exact_trace_residuals_intersect proof already supplies this correctly.

checks.method: Compared the changed Section4 sentence with singleton_trace_card_le_ten and exact_trace_residuals_intersect in frozen Erdos20RankFour.lean and Erdos20RankThree.lean.
checks.observation: For distinct residues P,Q from original members S,T with trace C={v}, disjointness implies S∩T=C, while S∩R=T∩R=C. The proof checks R≠S, R≠T and S≠T and then constructs {R,S,T}⊆H. The prose currently names P,Q,R instead; this needs the stated minor clarification.

checks.scope: Skeptical test of fixed-key fiber graph and cardinality preservation
checks.method: Read ProfileAFibers.fiber_card_le_four, fixed_pair_four_outsiders_card_le_four and residualLink_sunflowerFree; checked the original-member reconstruction and graph-degree argument.
checks.observation: Every member of a fiber contains the fixed two-set P, so deleting P is injective and the residual-link cardinality equals the fiber cardinality. Residual members are two-sets within the four-point outsider set. Any residual sunflower lifts by adjoining P, so sunflower-freeness transfers. Degree at most two then yields at most four edges by incidence; no separate assumption that the outsider graph is simple or sunflower-free is silently inserted.
